```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

We explored using sampling with replacement to get a sense of both the total number of individuals of each size sampled at the different stations in the EBS. Essentially it would incorporate both the abundance information and length information in the same place. 
However, we don't necessarily need/want that information in the same model (depending on our questions).

For now lets explore length models without accounting for total catch

```{r}
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# need to use world not world2hires cause that one is hella old and doesn't plot correctly
bs_map <- maps::map("world", regions = c("USA:Alaska", "Russia"), 
                    fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE, wrap = c(0, 360)) %>%
  st_as_sf(crs = 4326) 

# Use bounding box, have to add 360 to the bbox coords
# xmin = 185 (-175), xmax = 202 (-155)
bbox_360 <- st_bbox(c(xmin = 180, xmax = 210, ymin = 50, ymax = 68), 
                    crs = st_crs(bs_map))

# crop 
# Using st_make_valid helps w/ messy polys
bs_base <- bs_map %>% 
  st_make_valid() %>% 
  st_intersection(st_as_sfc(bbox_360)) %>%
  st_shift_longitude() 

bs_utm <- bs_base %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32602) # Move to UTM Zone 2N
  

#read in bathymetry file.

bathline.xyz <- as.xyz(bathline)
```

# 1. lng SDMtmb
```{r}
head(lngs)
# check for NAs
table(is.na(lngs$corrected_length)) # 17 true
table(is.na(lngs$eq_latitude))
table(is.na(lngs$eq_longitude))
table(is.na(lngs$haul_date))


lngs_utm <- lngs %>%
  # for now we'll remove the na lengths but ideally we'll fix this on the db side so it won't be a prblem
  filter(!(is.na(corrected_length))) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(haul_date),
         doy = yday(date),
         median_doy = median(doy),
         scale_doy = doy - median_doy,
         mean_doy = mean(doy),
         sd_doy = sd(doy),
         scale_doy2 = (doy - mean_doy)/sd_doy,
         scaled_median = (median_doy - mean_doy) / sd_doy) %>%
  arrange(station_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(sample_year, station_id, doy, scale_doy, scale_doy2, scaled_median, eq_latitude, eq_longitude, corrected_length)) %>%
  add_utm_columns(., ll_names = c("eq_longitude", "eq_latitude"),
                  ll_crs = 4326, utm_names = c("X", "Y"), 
                  units = "km") # uses crs 32602
  
# create mesh
mesh.lng <- make_mesh(lngs_utm, c("X", "Y"), n_knots = 75)
plot(mesh.lng)
```

# fit measured lengths

We have a couple options to how we fit this:
- we can use a gaussian 
- we can use a lognormal
- generalized gamma 
```{r}
fit.gaus <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = gaussian(),
  #family = lognormal(link = "log"), 
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

fit.logN <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

fit.gamma <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_utm,
  # model formula
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  # add mesh
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  # we want to fit a spatiotemporal model with iid so we need to say which is the time category
  time = "sample_year", 
  # family important.... start with gaussian
  family = gengamma(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  # each year independentally estimated
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  # we want ansiotropy because we want to assume that the decomposition of Matern distance isn't
  # necessarily the same EW as NS. Esp cause in the BS we have the shelf patterns that can drive 
  # species distributions
  anisotropy = TRUE
)
```


Do they all converge appropriately?
```{r}
sanity(fit.gaus)
sanity(fit.logN)
sanity(fit.gamma)

# all converge appropriately

AIC(fit.gaus); AIC(fit.logN); AIC(fit.gamma)

# generalized gamma has the lowest AIC

tidy(fit.gaus, "ran_pars") # is the wild sd scaled doy bc its gaussian?
tidy(fit.logN, "ran_pars") 
tidy(fit.gamma, "ran_pars")
```

## model evalutions
```{r}
# model list:
# already removed nbs pcod because that model doesn't converge nice
model.list <- list(fit.gaus, fit.logN, fit.gamma)
names(model.list) <- c("fit.gaus", "fit.logN", "fit.gamma")
```

### gradient check
```{r}
check_gradient <- function(model) {
  if(any(model$gradients > 0.0005)){
    print(paste("model has too large of a gradient:", names(model)))
  } else {
    print("model passes gradient check")
  }
}

for(i in 1:length(model.list)) {
  print(names(model.list)[[i]])
  check_gradient(model.list[[i]])
}
```

### residual plots
this takes longer to run since i'm simulating 500 times to then extract dharma residuals.
```{r}
# create empty plot list
residual.plots <- list()
spatial.plots <- list()
residual.df <- list()

# if underlying data changes (no longer lngs_utm) then this has to change

for(name in names(model.list)) {

  mod <- model.list[[name]]
  df <- lngs_utm
  
  # get model names
  mod_fam <- mod$family$family
  fam_label <- paste(mod_fam, collapse = "_")
  
  # extract residuals
  sims <- simulate(mod, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
  resid <- dharma_residuals(sims, mod, return_DHARMa = TRUE)
  
  # create dharma plots as ggplots
  p_qq <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotQQunif(resid))
  p_res <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotResiduals(resid))
  
  # combine residual plots
  dharma_plots <- wrap_plots(p_qq, p_res) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste(name, fam_label, "DHARMa Diagnostics"))
  
  # put plot in a list to look at
  residual.plots[[name]] <- dharma_plots
  
  # put the residuals in a df for spatial plotting
  df$resid <- resid$scaledResiduals
  residual.df[[name]] <- df
  
  # create spatial plot
  spatials <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_point(aes(X,Y, col = resid)) +
    labs(title = paste(name, fam_label, "Spatial residuals")) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~sample_year) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # put into list to look at
  spatial.plots[[name]] <- spatials
  


  print(name)
  residual.df[[name]] <- df
  
}
```

##cross validation
The fits of all the different distributions look fine. If you continue down the 
script we compare the partial effects of length by year at an average spatial location and median doy 248

However lets fint some cv models to see if we can definitely choose a model
```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
plan(multisession)

gaus_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = gaussian(),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  k_folds = 6
)

logN_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  k_folds = 6
)

gamma_cv <- sdmTMB_cv(
  data = lngs_utm,
  corrected_length ~ 0 + s(scale_doy2) + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = gengamma(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE, 
  k_folds = 6
)
```

Comparing outputs
```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
#1. compare the nge log likelihood - closer to 0 is better
gaus_cv$sum_loglik
logN_cv$sum_loglik 
gamma_cv$sum_loglik

#2. look at mean log likelihoods
mean_loglike_gaus <- gaus_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(gaus_cv$data) 
mean_loglike_logN <- logN_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(logN_cv$data)
mean_loglike_gamma <- gamma_cv$sum_loglik / nrow(gamma_cv$data)

#3. look at RMSE across entire dataset
sqrt(mean((gaus_cv$data$corrected_length - gaus_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 
sqrt(mean((logN_cv$data$corrected_length - logN_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 
sqrt(mean((gamma_cv$data$corrected_length - gamma_cv$data$cv_predicted)^2)) 

#4. RMSE by folds
rmse_gaus <- dplyr::group_by(gaus_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
rmse_logN <- dplyr::group_by(logN_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
rmse_gamma <- dplyr::group_by(gamma_cv$data, cv_fold) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(
    mae = mean(abs(corrected_length - cv_predicted)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((corrected_length - cv_predicted)^2)))
# hmm look the same
ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_gaus, col = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_logN, col = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(x = cv_fold, rmse), data = rmse_gamma, col = "green")

#' honestly hard to come up with a determination based on this, but the cross validation didn't seem to work super well with 
#' the gaussian distribution, the model doesn't convert with the different folds
#' the gamma seems to consistently have higher rmse so I t hink we'll split the diff and use the logN
```


create prediction
```{r}
# create prediction grid
## create sf object
lng_sf <- lngs_utm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(c(X, Y, eq_latitude, eq_longitude)) %>%
  mutate(X = X*1000, Y = Y*1000) %>% # convert to meters for crs 32602
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32602)

## create convex hull
convex <- concaveman(lng_sf, concavity = 3)

## add buffer to edges
convex_buff <- st_buffer(convex, dist = 15e3) # dist in meters (we think)
plot(convex_buff) # looks about right

## make grid
# make grid, created a cell size of 10,000 x 10,000 m (10 x 10 km) with poitns in center
# need to check units on this... 
grid <- st_make_grid(convex_buff, cellsize = 10e3, what = "centers") %>%
  st_intersection(convex_buff)

## change back to df
bs.grid <- do.call(rbind, st_geometry(grid)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>% setNames(c("X", "Y")) %>%
  # convert df m back to km
  mutate(X = X/1e3, Y = Y/1e3)
plot(bs.grid)

## replicate df across years and include any other variables we inlcude in our fit of the model
## i.e., depth tmeperature etc
scaled_median <- unique(lngs_utm$scaled_median)

bs.grid.year <- replicate_df(bs.grid, "sample_year", unique(lngs_utm$sample_year))
bs.grid.year.doy <- replicate_df(bs.grid.year, "scale_doy2", scaled_median) # this is at doy 248
```

predict back to observations

## index comparison

```{r}
# predict 
pred.gaus <- predict(fit.gaus, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")
pred.logN <- predict(fit.logN, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")
pred.gamma <- predict(fit.gamma, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy, return_tmb_object = T, type = "response")

# index
index.gaus <- get_index(pred.gaus, bias_correct = T)
index.logN <- get_index(pred.logN, bias_correct = T)
index.gamma <- get_index(pred.gamma, bias_correct = T)

# plot index and see how much they vary between distributions
ggplot() +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.gaus, aes(x = sample_year, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "blue") +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.logN, aes(x = sample_year+0.1, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "green") +
  geom_pointrange(data = index.gamma, aes(x = sample_year+0.5, y = est, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), color = "orange")
# the pattern is identical, the ci appears to be close (although some variation)
# the point estimates for gaussian are the lowest with logN slightly higher and gamma above that. 

library(ggeffects)
# marginal effect of sample_year holding DOY at median
eff.gaus <- ggpredict(fit.gaus, terms = "sample_year [all]")
eff.logN <- ggpredict(fit.logN, terms = "sample_year [all]")
eff.gamma <- ggpredict(fit.gamma, terms = "sample_year [all]")

eff.logN <- as.data.frame(eff.logN) %>%
  mutate(dist = "logN")
eff.gamma <- as.data.frame(eff.gamma) %>%
  mutate(dist = "gamma")

all.dat <- as.data.frame(eff.gaus) %>%
  mutate(dist = "gaussian") %>%
  rbind(eff.logN) %>%
  rbind(eff.gamma)

ggplot(all.dat) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x= x, y = predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, color = dist), position = position_jitter()) +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Predicted length (mm)")

ggplot(eff.logN) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(x= x, y = predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  labs(x = "Years", y = "Predicted length (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Predicted mapping

## deviations from average
```{r}
# have to predict the correct model again but not keep the tmb object
pred <- predict(fit.logN, newdata = bs.grid.year.doy)

# create a sf of the predictions
pred.lng.sf <- pred %>%
  mutate(Y = Y*1000,
         X = X*1000) %>% # sf requires meters
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32602) %>%
  st_transform(., crs = 4326) %>%
  st_shift_longitude()
  
# what might be helpful here too is the average spatial field 
#' by keeping the exp(omega) were showing the relative length anomaly across space. 
#' here (I think) it means that 1 is the average or baseline value (aka average length of a fish after accounting for doy & ran eff maybe)
#' the larger and smaller deviations are above and below 1. So 1.075 representes a fish that is 7.5% larger than the average
#' math: percent increase = exp(value) -1 * 100
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bs_cropped_wgs, fill = "gray", color = "black", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = exp(omega_s), color = exp(omega_s)),
          data = pred.lng.sf, pch = 22) +
  geom_contour(data = bathline, aes(x = x +360, y = y, z = z),
               breaks = c(-20, -50, -100, -150), linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

#' if we wanted to know what the absolute length deviations from a fish you'd need to incorporate the average length of a fish
mean(exp(pred$est)) # I dunno if this is legit but for now lets call an average fish is 57 mm long
pred.lng.sf$absolute_omega_s <- (exp(pred.lng.sf$omega_s) - 1) * (mean(exp(pred$est)))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bs_cropped_wgs, fill = "gray", color = "black", inherit.aes = F) +
  geom_sf(mapping = aes(fill = absolute_omega_s, color = absolute_omega_s),
          data = pred.lng.sf, pch = 22) +
  geom_contour(data = bathline, aes(x = x +360, y = y, z = z),
               breaks = c(-20, -50, -100, -150), linewidth = 0.3, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = expression("Deviation from \naverage length (mm)"),
       fill = expression("Deviation from \naverage length (mm)"))
```

# Env models
Okay and close to the those particular length sdmTMB models. 
What does it look like to add in additional parameters to the model formula? 

Starting with the simple ones, temperature/coldpoolindex
```{r}
head(lngs_utm)
head(cold_pool_index)
cpi <- rename_with(cold_pool_index, tolower)

# these are the matched mom6 but it doesn't have the 2026 data
lng_moms <- read.csv("Data/pollock_corrected_lngs_wMOM6.csv") %>%
  dplyr::select(c(sample_year, haul_date, eq_latitude, eq_longitude, region,
                  corrected_length, mean_bottom_temp, mean_surface_temp)) %>%
  mutate(sample_year = as.numeric(sample_year)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(mean_mom6_surface_temp = mean_surface_temp,
                mean_mom6_bottom_temp = mean_bottom_temp) %>%
  # add a unique ID year for ease of joining
  arrange(sample_year, eq_latitude, eq_longitude, corrected_length) %>%
  mutate(unique_id = 1:nrow(.))

lngs_env <- lngs_utm %>%
  left_join(cpi, by = c("sample_year" = "year")) %>%
  mutate(sc_surf_tmp = scale(mean_surface_temperature),
         sample_year = as.numeric(sample_year))
  
poll_temp <- lngs_env %>% 
  # remove 2026 since we have no mom data
  arrange(., sample_year, eq_latitude, eq_longitude, corrected_length) %>%
  mutate(unique_id = 1:nrow(.)) %>%
  filter(sample_year != 2026) %>%
  left_join(lng_moms, by = c("unique_id", "sample_year", "eq_latitude", "eq_longitude", "corrected_length"))

# scale temp
poll_temp$scale_mom_surf <- scale(poll_temp$mean_mom6_surface_temp, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
```


```{r}
#' what do we think we're fitting here? 
#' looking at the spatial/spatiotemporal patterns in length of pollock when accounting for yearly
#' variability in surface temperature and doy

fit.stmp <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_env,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + s(mean_surface_temperature, k = 4),
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "off",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

fit.stmp2 <- sdmTMB(
  data = lngs_env,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + mean_surface_temperature,
  mesh = mesh.lng, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "off",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

# raster style fit - have to recreate mesh without 2026
# create mesh
mesh_temp <- make_mesh(poll_temp, c("X", "Y"), n_knots = 75)

fit.mom <- sdmTMB(
  data = poll_temp,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + as.factor(sample_year) + scale_mom_surf,
  mesh = mesh_temp, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

# add in spline to test for nonlinear effects of temperature
fit.mom.spline <- sdmTMB(
  data = poll_temp,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + as.factor(sample_year) + s(scale_mom_surf, k = 4),
  mesh = mesh_temp, 
  time = "sample_year", 
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

# add in a base sdmtmb model without temperature effects
base.fit <- sdmTMB(
  data = poll_temp,
  corrected_length ~ scale_doy2 + as.factor(sample_year),
  mesh = mesh_temp,
  time = "sample_year",
  family = lognormal(link = "log"),
  spatial = "on",
  spatiotemporal = "IID",
  anisotropy = TRUE
)

sanity(fit.mom)
sanity(fit.mom.spline)
sanity(base.fit)
sanity(fit.stmp)
sanity(fit.stmp2)

tidy(fit.stmp, "ran_pars"); tidy(fit.stmp2, "ran_pars")
tidy(fit.stmp); tidy(fit.stmp2)

check_gradient(fit.stmp); check_gradient(fit.stmp2)
check_gradient(fit.mom); check_gradient(fit.mom.spline)
check_gradient(base.fit)
tidy(fit.mom)

AIC(fit.stmp2) - AIC(fit.stmp)
# this indicates that a spline temperature inclusion is probably better
# looking at the moms data and inclusion of nonlinear temperature effects
AIC(base.fit, fit.mom.spline) # base fit is larger than spline
AIC(base.fit) - AIC(fit.mom) # the base fit and the temperature mom is pretty similar
AIC(fit.mom) - AIC(fit.mom.spline) # there is stronger support for a model with temperature effects
# but primarily non linear effect of temperature. 

print(tidy(fit.mom.spline, "fixed"), n = 24) # the scaled temperature overlaps with 0 
# so there while the inclusion of temperature better fits the model there is not a significant impact of temperature on length
# after accounting for variability across space, year, and doy

# how much does the model improve when temperature is included? 
# we can look at the spatial field (sigma_0) and the spatiotemporal fields (sigma_E)
# and compare with the base model to look at if there's a decrease in sigma_0
# if decrease in sigma_o then *i think* it'd mean there's a spatial pattern in lengths that is driven by
# spatial temperature differences. 
tidy(base.fit, "ran_pars")
tidy(fit.mom.spline, "ran_pars")
# from the base.fit (w/o temp) sigma_O is 0.0582, w/ temp is 0.0711
# so there is an increase in sigma_0 when temperature is included.
# this means that the baseline spatial standar deviation increased when temperature was included. 
# This means that after accounting for temperature, there's more residual variabiltiy associated with 
# peristent other features in the bering sea (depth, habitat, ontogeny, prey) well maybe nto really prey
# WHY would that happen? 
# However both sigma_O parameters are within the sd of the other - it wasn't a statistical increase/decrease
# in the persistent spatial pattern of pollock lengths

# the sigma_E didn't chang from the base to the temp model, but the magniture of the parameter is large. 
# indicating there is a year to year variation in the spatial length patterns of pollock. 
# so there is something that is happening year to year that is not a persistent underlying pattern that more 
#larger impacts where we find larger/small pollock in the Bering sea. 
# becasue the inclusion of temperature didn't change hte sigma_E something else is driving the interannual variability we see
# across space and size in the EBS
```

### model eval
```{r}
mod <- fit.stmp 
df <- lngs_env
  # extract residuals
  sims <- simulate(mod, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
  resid <- dharma_residuals(sims, mod, return_DHARMa = TRUE)
  
  # create dharma plots as ggplots
  p_qq <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotQQunif(resid))
  p_res <- as.grob(~DHARMa::plotResiduals(resid))
  
  # combine residual plots
  dharma_plots <- wrap_plots(p_qq, p_res) +
    plot_annotation(title = paste(name, fam_label, "DHARMa Diagnostics"))
  
  # view
  dharma_plots
  
  # put the residuals in a df for spatial plotting
  df$resid <- resid$scaledResiduals
  
  # create spatial plot
  spatials <- ggplot(df) +
    geom_point(aes(X,Y, col = resid)) +
    labs(title =  "Spatial residuals") +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~sample_year) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal()

  # view 
  spatials
```

### predict temp grids x year
```{r}
tos <- readRDS("C:/Users/lia.domke/Desktop/Work/AFSC/R projects/BSpcod-lengths/tos_MOM6_1993_2025_AK.rds") %>%
  rename(surface_temp = bottom_temp)

tos$lon <- ifelse(tos$lon > 180, tos$lon - 360, tos$lon)

tos_summer <- tos %>%
    filter(month == "06"| month == "07"| month == "08" )%>%
    filter(lon >= -180 & lon <= -130,
           lat >= 50 & lat <= 70,
           year > 2002) %>%
    group_by(year, lon, lat) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_surf_temp = mean(surface_temp, na.rm = T),
                   sd_surf_temp = sd(surface_temp, na.rm = T), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

# convert tos to sf and make sure the epsg matches the bs.grid (32602), the grid is calculated in meters
tos_summer_sf <- st_as_sf(tos_summer, coords = c("lon", "lat"),
                          crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32602)

# pull out coordinates
coords_tos <- st_coordinates(tos_summer_sf)
tos_summer_m <- tos_summer %>%
  mutate(X = coords_tos[, "X"] / 1000,
         Y = coords_tos[, "Y"] / 1000)

head(tos_summer_m)

# pull out the mean and sd of mom6 temp from the matched station grids
surf_mean <- mean(poll_temp$mean_mom6_surface_temp, na.rm = T)
surf_sd <- sd(poll_temp$mean_mom6_surface_temp, na.rm = T)

poll_temp2 <- poll_temp %>%
  mutate(scale_mom_surf = as.numeric(scale_mom_surf)) %>%
  mutate(scale_mom_surf2 = (mean_mom6_surface_temp - surf_mean)/ surf_sd,
         matches = dplyr::near(scale_mom_surf, scale_mom_surf2))

table(poll_temp2$matches) # good

#check to make sure its all projected correctly
# ggplot() +
#   geom_point(tos_summer_m, mapping = aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = mean_surf_temp)) +
#   geom_point(lngs_utm, mapping = aes(x = X, y = Y), fill = "red")


# previous prediction grid
bs.grid.year.doy <- replicate_df(bs.grid.year, "scale_doy2", scaled_median) # this is at doy 248

pred_years <- intersect(unique(bs.grid.year.doy$sample_year), unique(tos_summer_m$year))
# prediction grid and include tos
grid_list <- list()

for (yr in sort(pred_years)) {
  grid_yr <- bs.grid.year.doy %>% filter(sample_year == yr)
  temp_yr <- tos_summer_m %>% filter(year == yr)
  
  # Nearest-neighbor lookup in EPSG:32602 km space
  nn <- FNN::get.knnx(
    data  = as.matrix(temp_yr[, c("X", "Y")]),
    query = as.matrix(grid_yr[, c("X", "Y")]),
    k     = 1
  )
  
  grid_yr$scale_mom_surf <- temp_yr$scale_mom_surf[nn$nn.index]
  grid_yr$mean_surf_temp <- temp_yr$mean_surf_temp[nn$nn.index]
  grid_yr$dist_to_mom6_km  <- nn$nn.dist[, 1]
  
  grid_list[[as.character(yr)]] <- grid_yr
}

bs.grid.temp <- bind_rows(grid_list) %>%
  mutate(scale_surf_temp = (mean_surf_temp - surf_mean) / surf_sd)

range(bs.grid.temp$dist_to_mom6_km) # 26 is kinda far, but the buffer is 15 km
# Check percentiles — 95% of the grid is ~ 6.2 km away
quantile(bs.grid.temp$dist_to_mom6_km, probs = c(0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 1.0))

# Plot the points > 15 km away to verify they are just coastal edge cells
ggplot(bs.grid.temp %>% filter(sample_year == 2021), aes(X, Y, color = dist_to_mom6_km > 15)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  coord_equal() # only a few locations around looks like nunivak island maybe st. lawrence that makes
# sense given that the mom6 is not calculated on land

```
